label: forge v2 greenfield (sans-IO kernel) — head-to-head vs v1
source: automated — sequential runs, isolated parent dirs + cleared state per tool; v1 via --prompt --verbose footer, v2 via forge run --json (v2 cost computed from usage at $3/$15/$0.30/$3.75 per M, same rates v1 prices with)

C1_lruCache.qualityNotes: Same sentinel DLL + Map core, but a verified artifact: clean compile on TS 6, 40/40, reproducible build (lockfile, @types/node), rigorous assertThrows harness. Deductions: has()/delete()/entries() scope creep (~9 assertions on unrequested surface); dead guard in _evictLRU; DOM lib in a Node project.

C2_rateLimiter.qualityNotes: Number.isFinite validation everywhere; documented RangeError on tokens>capacity (avoids v1's forever-false trap); 5 assertThrows failure-path tests. Caveats: one async test never awaited (its assertion can't fail the suite); tsconfig include skips the test file so tests are never type-checked; no injectable clock.

C3_eventEmitter.qualityNotes: Strong compile-time story (interface event maps accepted, all negative probes rejected). Runtime fails 4/6 adversarial probes: off() cannot cancel once() (wrapper identity bug contradicting its own JSDoc); live-Set iteration lets listeners added during emit fire in the same emit (100-deep re-entrancy confirmed); duplicate on() silently dedupes. Its 5 tests never touch the broken cases.

overallQuality.basis: 4 graded units (3 complex head-to-head + simple tier), restraint-weighted adversarial rubric
strengths: every artifact verified in-session (3/3 compile clean, all delivered tests pass)
strict input validation + documented error contracts
weaknesses: turn inflation: 1.6-5x v1 turns from compulsive full-project scaffolding
scope creep on simple prompts (restraint penalty)
real bugs the self-tests never touch: once/off wrapper identity, live-Set re-entrancy, palindrome default
